newsitem.title: USA: Footstar shares slump after outlook.
newsitem.headline: Footstar shares slump after outlook.

text.p: Shares of Footstar Inc were shaved 24 percent after the company posted better-than-expected first quarter earnings but said it sees signs of slowing in recent sales of the athletic sector overall.
The stock fell 6-1/8 to 19 in heavy trading with the stock the top loser on the New York Stock Exchange on a percentage basis.

Shares touched a new year low of 18-1/2 in intraday trading. Footstar, which operates nearly 500 Footaction athletic footwear stores, posted earnings per share of $0.16 compared with $0.03 on a pro forma basis. According to First Call, Wall Street analysts expected earnings of $0.09.

But in the earnings release, Footstar chairman and chief executive Mickey Robinson said on the heels of a strong 1996, "recent sales trends and the athletic sector in general have shown signs of slowing."

"However, we have planned conservatively and expect Footstar to deliver bottom-line results for the year as anticipated through effective cost control and inventory management," he said in the statement.
The Mahwah, N.J.-company also operates about 2,500 footwear departments in Meldisco.
